doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Alto sound, teachers and fellow altoists
title: Other altoists: Ornette, Bartz, Desmond, Coleman, Lake, Jenkins, Sharpe
summary: McLean gives quick opinions on Ornette Coleman, Gary Bartz, Desmond, Kenny Garrett, Steve Coleman, Oliver Lake, John Jenkins and Cee Sharpe.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Okay. Do you know Earl Turbinton?
No.
Doesn’t mean anything to you?
No.
Ornette [Coleman].
Yeah, I like Ornette. He’s a good alto player. I like him because he stood his ground and took the slings and arrows when it was a real hard time for him to do what he
Gary Bartz.
I like Gary a lot. One of my favorite alto players.
What – did you have a relationship with him? I know you recorded with him, but the . . .

Yeah, we had a relationship, because he – I used to let him sit in with me when he first was coming to New York and trying to make a name for himself. He would always come to my gig. He knew he could sit in, play with me.
Paul Desmond.
Yeah, I liked him. I respect him and appreciate him more now than I did when I was coming up. For that sound, I like Lee Konitz much more. But I liked Paul Desmond. He was a good saxophone . . .
You mean that sound like that light, almost airy kind of sound?
Yeah, the light approach to . . .
Which is kind of the opposite of the force that . . .

Right, that I play and that Bird played. But it’s come back again. A lot of alto players now got that light, very – Gary Bartz. Not Gary Bartz. Kenny Garrett has a very light, airy sound, and so do a lot of alto players out there today.
Steve Coleman.
I like him. He’s a fine young alto player. Yeah, I think he’s a comer. Plays real good.
What about people like Oliver Lake, Julius Hemphill?

I like them for their honesty and that they do what they do. I like Oliver especially, because Oliver will tell you in a minute that he tried to play like me. He tried to play like Bird. He used to say that he likes me a lot. Tried to get my records and play like me. He just couldn’t do it. He said then he found a way to make his expression, and I think it’s very – it’s great.
What about alto players that we may – nobody may have heard of, but you think are burners?
John Jenkins was a great alto player from Chicago. He and I made some records together. I liked John.
Right, with Alto Madness being the one that I know.

Yeah. He made some other ones on Blue Note. I liked them a lot. Cee Sharpe, Clarence Sharpe. I thought he was a magnificent alto player. He made some records and did some things, but he never got the kind of recognition that I thought he should have gotten.
